cases.expected: Row fields (requirement id/text/type/status, meeting, story id/title/text, priority, ACs) equal the Component 1 item.

cases.title: Component 2 test cases linked to the correct requirement
cases.objective: Verify each Component 2 test case is attached only to the requirement whose user_story_id equals the test's story_id.
cases.expected: R1 (story S1) gets T1 and T2; R2 (story S2) gets only T3; no test appears under the wrong requirement.

cases.title: Unmatched test case (story not in Component 1)
cases.objective: Verify a Component 2 test case whose story_id does not exist in the Component 1 iteration is not linked to any requirement and is not counted.
cases.expected: Orphan test absent from all rows; summary total_tests counts only linked tests.

cases.title: Requirement with no linked test case
cases.objective: Verify a requirement with no Component 2 test case is reported as NOT COVERED.
cases.expected: coverage_status = NOT COVERED, total_tests = 0, coverage_pct = 0, every AC listed as missing.

cases.title: Partially covered requirement
cases.objective: Verify a requirement whose tests cover only some acceptance criteria is PARTIAL and lists the uncovered criteria.
cases.expected: 2 of 3 ACs covered -> PARTIAL, coverage 66.7%, missing = the account-lockout criterion.
cases.actual: status=PARTIAL; covered 2/3 (66.7%); missing=['The account is locked after five failed login attempts']

cases.title: Fully covered requirement
cases.objective: Verify a requirement whose linked tests cover every acceptance criterion is FULLY COVERED.
cases.expected: coverage_status = FULLY COVERED, coverage_pct = 100, no missing ACs.

cases.title: Requirement with no acceptance criteria (incomplete traceability data)
cases.objective: Document how the RTM treats a requirement that arrives from Component 1 with an empty acceptance-criteria list.
cases.expected: Implemented behaviour: with >=1 linked test the row is FULLY COVERED at 100% (nothing to miss); with no test it is NOT COVERED.

evidence.label: Note
evidence.value: A requirement with no acceptance criteria cannot be checked at AC level, so any linked test makes it 'fully covered'. Reviewers should treat such rows as a data-quality issue in Component 1.

cases.title: RTM summary aggregates
cases.objective: Verify the matrix summary counts requirements by status, tests by result, pass rate over executed tests, and average coverage.
cases.expected: 3 requirements (1 full, 1 partial, 1 not covered); 3 tests: 1 passed, 1 failed, 1 pending; pass rate 50%; defects 1; avg coverage = mean of row coverage.

cases.title: Execution status derived from Component 2 results
cases.objective: Verify Component 2's traceability payload is mapped to test status using only ACTIVE suites and only the LATEST execution, matching scenario titles by word overlap.
cases.expected: Gherkin A: latest run of active suite passed -> approved (older failure ignored); Gherkin B: failed in latest run -> rejected; Gherkin C: only in an inactive suite -> pending; Gherkin D: no matching result -> pending.

cases.title: Generated gap test cases merged into the RTM
cases.objective: Verify a gap test case added to the RTM appears in its requirement row with source = generated and contributes to coverage.
cases.expected: Row contains the generated test (id gap-<n>, source generated); lockout AC becomes covered.
cases.actual: Before: PARTIAL 66.7% tests=['T1']; After: FULLY COVERED 100.0% tests=[('T1', 'C2'), ('gap-1', 'generated')]

cases.title: Requirement detail lookup
cases.objective: Verify the requirement-detail endpoint returns the matching row and 404 for an unknown requirement.
cases.expected: Known id -> 200 with that requirement; unknown id -> 404 'Requirement not found in this iteration'.
cases.actual: R1 -> 200 (R1); NOPE -> 404 {'detail': 'Requirement not found in this iteration'}

cases.title: Two requirements sharing one user story
cases.objective: Document the implemented behaviour when Component 1 links two requirements to the same user story.
cases.expected: Both requirement rows list the story's test cases (traceability is via the shared story).
